newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, wait for rain.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, wait for rain.

text.p: Polish shares on Thursday extended Wednesday's gains in stable turnover and analysts said the market would be watching to what degree forecasts of more heavy rain in coming days would come true.
On Thursday Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz warned parliament that weather forecasts showed heavy rain overnight and may cause a new wave of floods in the country's south.

"Current gains are a reaction to recent falls but the mood is pretty jittery with forecasts of more rain, which could have an effect tomorrow," said Janusz Oleksak, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
Before the current rises the market had fallen 5.2 percent over three sessions, a loss deepened by flood concerns.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.9 percent to 15,406.1 points and turnover was flat at 208.2 million zlotys ($59.5 million) on both markets. Gainers led losers by 61 to 25 with 20 stocks flat.
Analysts said builders and furniture makers seen benefiting from post-flood demand.
They said top gainer cable maker BFK, up the daily maximum 10 percent in light trade, benefited from strong June earnings data released on Wednesday.

But analysts said overall market gains could prove short-lived not only by rising flood waters but on concerns on the degree to which Poland's planned 2.8-percent 1997 budget deficit might be affected by flood relief aid.
Analysts also said the zloty's recent volality did not put investors in a buying mood though the finance minister said on Thursday it was caused by speculation by Polish traders and should soon firm.
